To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the induction of a delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction to azoben-zene-arsonate (ABA) was achieved by the injection of a monoclonal antibody (Mab) directed against an idiotype on ABA-specific antibodies of A/J (H-2a) mice.
a monoclonal reagent, 1A, directed against an idiotype of ABA-specific antibodies of A/J strain mice induced delayed hypersensitivity to ABA in A/J mice.

a monoclonal antibody directed to an idiotypic determinant of anti-ABA antibodies induced delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) to ABA, and the T cells mediating DTH were restricted by the K-region of the H-2 complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an anti-idiotype which can induce an immune response to the original antigen.
the use of monoclonal anti-idiotypic antibodies to induce delayed-type hypersensitivity.
the induction of delayed-type hypersensitivities by monoclonal antibodies directed against idiotopes of anti-hapten antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the monoclonal antibody 14A induced a T-cell-dependent, K-end-restricted ABA-specific delayed-type hypersensitivity response in A/J mice.
a single idiotype can induce a delayed hypersensitivity reaction to a hapten.
the 14A idiotype is a determinant of the T cell receptor, not of the antibody.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the idiotype network can function as an antigen.
the anti-idiotypic antibody 14A can induce A/J mice to be ABA-specific, that this is mediated by a T cell response and that it is restricted by the K-antigen of the major histo-compatibility complex.
14A, which is a monoclonal antibody, is able to induce a delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) to ABA in A/J mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-idiotype 14A, by virtue of its cross-reactivity with anti-ABA antibodies, can mimic ABA and induce delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) to it.
we were able to induce a delayed-type hypersensitivity response in mice to an antigen that the mice were not sensitized to.
the induction of delayed type hypersensitivity to ABA by 14A is mediated by T cells and that the 14A idiotype is involved in the induction of T cell help for the anti-ABA response.
